text:
If you only saw the shot clock, you would have picked the wrong team. The Kings threw 69 attempts at Ilya Sorokin to the Islanders' 37, out-hit them 33 to 9 and built 3.18 expected goals (the quality of their chances) to 2.02. Our replays of every shot give Los Angeles this game 80% of the time. The Islanders won it 5-2, and snapped a four-game winless run (0-2-2) doing it.

The difference was at both ends of the ice in the worst way for the Kings. Darcy Kuemper allowed four goals on 20 shots, about 2.5 more than those shots deserved. Matthew Schaefer, the most written-about Islander of the last two weeks, scored on a 4% power-play chance in the first period, and that was the night in miniature. Schaefer logged 27 minutes, and the goal pushed New York's win chance from 51% to 67%.

Los Angeles owned the second period, 1.58 to 0.48 in expected goals, but only had Quinton Byfield's power-play goal at 7:52 to show for it, set up by Artemi Panarin and Kevin Fiala. That pulled the Kings within 3-2 after Victor Eklund had made it 3-1 earlier in the period. Then Simon Holmstrom scored 39 seconds into the third, and New York's chances jumped from 73% to 89%. Erik Haula had the best look left for the Kings, a 27% chance early in the third, and it didn't go in. Bo Horvat closed it at 17:14, his 18th point, which NHL.com's Stefen Rosner noted matches Schaefer.

Brayden Schenn was first star with a goal and two assists, and the early goal at 5:50 was his. The most encouraging line in the box score might be Ryan Pulock's two assists: Pulock and Matias Maccelli were both back on this West Coast trip after injuries, and Maccelli set up Schaefer's goal. Sorokin finished with 26 saves and 1.18 goals saved above expected. The Islanders were outplayed and they will take it anyway. For the Kings, losing a game this lopsided in their favour is the kind that stings in March.
headline: Islanders get outplayed in LA, and win anyway
